screening_decisions.reason: Retrospective cohort study of 55 children treated with nephrectomy for Wilms tumor. Reports on long-term renal function (GFR) with median follow-up of 7-11 years. Meets all criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrectomy treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.

Study reports on TBI-related toxicities in ALL patients but does not report on renal function outcomes. Main late toxicities mentioned are cataract, growth, gonadal and endocrine effects. No renal function data reported, so cannot be included for this renal-focused review.

Study of 72 patients after ABMT (41 with TBI). Reports on renal function (GFR, creatinine, urea). While primary assessment was at 6 months, abstract mentions 'some patients have later improved considerably' suggesting longer follow-up. TBI involves kidney region. Conservative inclusion due to potential long-term data.

Retrospective study of 71 children with Wilms tumor focusing on clinical presentation, tumor characteristics, and surgical approaches. Does not report on renal function outcomes post-treatment. No data on GFR, creatinine, or other renal function markers.

Broad study of 519 pediatric cancer survivors assessing all adverse health conditions using CTCAE grading. Not specifically focused on renal function outcomes. Treatment modalities not specified, and renal outcomes not highlighted. Does not meet specific renal function reporting criteria.

Study comparing racial/ethnic differences in late outcomes among CCS. Reports on mortality, subsequent neoplasms, and chronic health conditions but does not specifically report on renal function outcomes. Not focused on nephrotoxic treatments or renal outcomes.

Study of 107 adult patients undergoing radical nephrectomy for cortical renal tumors. Not childhood cancer survivors - patients are adults with renal cell carcinoma. Does not meet population criteria (treated before age 21 for childhood cancer).

Review article providing recommendations for general practitioners managing adult childhood cancer survivors. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function. Does not report specific renal outcomes or meet study design criteria.

Retrospective study of 92 children (≤16 years) who underwent TBI before allogeneic SCT. 43 patients had ≥12 months follow-up (median 51 months). Reports on renal dysfunction defined by serum creatinine. TBI involves kidney region. Meets all criteria: childhood cancer survivors, radiation involving kidney region, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.

Study focuses on ACUTE renal toxicity in the early post-transplant period, not long-term outcomes ≥1 year after treatment cessation. Population appears to be adults (not specified as children). Does not meet the criterion of reporting renal function one year or longer after cessation of treatment.

Study of 23 children with Wilms tumor receiving high-dose chemotherapy including carboplatin. Median observation 41 months. Reports on renal toxicity (tubular dysfunction). While renal function monitoring was during treatment, the study follows patients long-term. Conservative inclusion as it reports on renal outcomes in childhood cancer survivors treated with carboplatin.

Study of 133 long-term survivors (>5 years) of extremity bone sarcoma. Median follow-up 12 years. Reports that 13% had reduced renal function. Osteosarcoma and Ewing sarcoma treatments typically include cisplatin and ifosfamide. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, >20 participants, renal function reported >1 year post-treatment.

Review article discussing management strategies for optic-hypothalamic gliomas in children. Mentions carboplatin and vincristine as treatments but does not report on renal function outcomes. Not a primary research study with original data.

Diagnostic accuracy study comparing cystatin C vs creatinine for GFR estimation in 68 children with malignancy. Focuses on measurement methodology rather than long-term renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment. Treatment modalities not specified, and study does not report on renal function ≥1 year after treatment cessation.

Report from NWTS database identifying 55 children who developed chronic renal failure during/after Wilms tumor treatment. Median interval from diagnosis to RF onset was 21 months (>1 year). Etiologies include bilateral nephrectomy, radiation nephritis. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrectomy/radiation treatments, >20 participants, renal outcomes reported.

Study of 22 children receiving cisplatin for neuroblastoma or germ cell tumors. Reports on GFR and creatinine measurements. However, abstract does not indicate that renal function was assessed ≥1 year after treatment cessation. Appears to focus on acute/subacute renal toxicity during treatment. Unclear if long-term outcomes reported.

Study of only 12 children assessed 1 and 10 years after ifosfamide treatment. Reports on chronic nephrotoxicity including glomerular and tubular dysfunction. However, sample size of 12 is fewer than 20 participants, which is an exclusion criterion.

Study of 28 children receiving cisplatin, focusing on prevention of hypomagnesemia. While hypomagnesemia can indicate tubular dysfunction, the study does not report on comprehensive renal function outcomes (GFR, proteinuria, etc.). Primary focus is on magnesium supplementation timing, not long-term renal outcomes ≥1 year post-treatment.

Phase III study of 188 patients with posterior fossa PNETs analyzing patterns of failure and prognostic factors. Does not report on renal function outcomes. Focus is on tumor recurrence and survival, not late effects or renal toxicity.

Systematic review evaluating frequency and risk factors of anthracycline-induced clinical heart failure in children. Focus is on cardiac toxicity, not renal function. Does not report on renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatments.

Very brief abstract mentioning ifosfamide use in childhood tumors. No sample size provided, no renal function outcomes reported. Appears to be a brief report or review without original data on long-term renal effects.
Study of 155 adult patients with renal cell carcinoma undergoing radical nephrectomy. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

Study comparing NF1 and non-NF1 children treated with carboplatin and vincristine for low-grade glioma. Reports on tumor responses, survival, and toxicities but does not specifically report on renal function outcomes. No renal function data mentioned.

Study of 26 patients with osteosarcoma treated with cisplatin and ifosfamide. Median follow-up 100 months. Reports only on acute nephrotoxicity during therapy (2 patients), not on long-term renal function outcomes ≥1 year after treatment cessation. Does not meet criterion for reporting renal function one year or longer after treatment.
Study of 28 adult patients with neuroendocrine tumors receiving PRRT. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria (treated before age 21 for childhood cancer).

Study of 31 children with stage 4 neuroblastoma, but only 16 survivors were evaluated for late effects including renal changes. Sample size of 16 survivors with renal outcome data is fewer than 20 participants. Does not meet minimum sample size criterion.

Study of 64 patients receiving ifosfamide with or without cisplatin. Reports on glomerular and tubular function after completion of chemotherapy. While timing of assessment is not explicitly stated as >1 year, the study evaluates renal toxicity after treatment completion. Conservative inclusion as it reports on renal function after nephrotoxic treatment.
Methodological article describing cohort study design. Not a primary research study with data on renal function in childhood cancer survivors.
Study of 347 nephrectomies in a general population (not specified as children). Not focused on childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

Study of 30 patients with poor-risk germ cell tumors receiving M-TIP regimen. Population appears to be adults (not specified as children). Does not meet population criteria for childhood cancer survivors (treated before age 21).

Study developing the CKD-EPI equation for estimating GFR in general population. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or nephrotoxic treatment effects. Does not meet population or intervention criteria.

Study of 28 children with Wilms tumor who developed renal failure during treatment. Focuses on chemotherapy dosing strategies during renal failure and survival outcomes, not on long-term renal function ≥1 year after treatment cessation. Does not report on renal function outcomes after treatment completion.

Study of 183 children with stage 4 neuroblastoma receiving cisplatin-based induction. Reports on acute nephrotoxicity during treatment (renal clearance), not on long-term renal function ≥1 year after treatment cessation. Does not meet criterion for long-term renal outcomes.

Phase III trial of 618 patients with osteosarcoma (age ≤40 years) comparing chemotherapy regimens. Reports on hematologic and non-hematologic toxicities but does not specifically report on renal function outcomes. No renal function data mentioned in abstract.

National survey of 142 patients (79 survivors) treated for solid malignant tumors before age 1 year. Mean follow-up 20 years. Reports renal damage as one of late side effects. Includes patients treated with nephrectomy, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, >20 participants, long-term follow-up, renal outcomes reported.

Study evaluating nephrotoxicity in patients under 21 years treated with ifosfamide-containing chemotherapy for rhabdomyosarcoma. Abstract is truncated but indicates focus on renal toxicity after ifosfamide treatment. Conservative inclusion as it appears to report on renal outcomes in childhood cancer survivors treated with ifosfamide.
Review article discussing radiation-induced renal toxicity. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function in childhood cancer survivors.
Case report of a single patient with cisplatin-induced hypomagnesemia and cardiac dysrhythmia. Case reports are excluded per selection criteria. Does not meet minimum sample size criterion.

Study of 35 adult survivors (mean age 25 years, mean follow-up 20 years) of unilateral non-syndromic renal tumors treated according to SIOP protocols. Reports on eGFR categories, CKD, and hypertension. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors (treated as children), nephrectomy treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.

Study of 1693 HCT patients evaluating CKD frequency. Population includes both adults and children with hematologic and nonhematologic disorders. Not specifically focused on childhood cancer survivors. Treatment modalities and age distribution unclear. Does not clearly meet population criteria.

Cochrane Review evaluating hepatic (liver) late adverse effects after childhood cancer treatment. Not focused on renal function outcomes. Does not report on renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatments.

Study of 144 adult patients with testicular germ cell tumors evaluating renal function after chemotherapy. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria (treated before age 21 for childhood cancer).

Study of 55 children receiving single fraction TBI before allogeneic SCT. Reports on early outcomes including acute renal failure (4%), but does not report on long-term renal function ≥1 year after treatment. Median follow-up 18.5 months but focus is on early outcomes.

Study of 30 children with abdominal neuroblastoma receiving definitive RT. Median follow-up 53 months. Reports on late kidney toxicity (2 patients with ipsilateral kidney hypoplasia). Radiation involves kidney region. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, radiation involving kidney region, >20 participants, renal outcomes reported >1 year post-treatment.

Study of 22 patients with bilateral Wilms tumor comparing bilateral partial nephrectomy vs unilateral partial plus contralateral total nephrectomy. Reports on renal hypertension outcomes. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrectomy treatment, >20 participants, renal outcomes (hypertension) reported.

Review article discussing late effects after stem cell transplantation. Mentions kidneys as one of affected organs but does not provide original data on renal function outcomes. Not a primary research study.
Study about hepatocellular carcinoma with no abstract available. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or renal function after nephrotoxic treatment. Does not meet criteria.

Study of 37 subjects who underwent unilateral nephrectomy during childhood (age <16 years). Long-term follow-up ranging from 0.5 to >20 years. Reports on GFR, renal plasma flow, and renal reserve capacity. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors (nephrectomy for renal tumors), nephrectomy treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.
Study of 163 adult patients with Stage I testicular seminoma. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.
Review article providing an overview of Wilms tumor disease characteristics, diagnosis, and testing. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.

Study of 33 childhood AML/myelodysplasia survivors. Reports abnormalities of renal function in both treatment groups (chemotherapy alone vs chemotherapy+TBI+BMT). Mean follow-up 7 years. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, >20 participants, renal function reported >1 year post-treatment. TBI involves kidney region.

Study of 24 children/adolescents with osteosarcoma treated with ifosfamide and cisplatin. Renal function assessed at least 3 months after treatment completion, not ≥1 year. Does not meet criterion of reporting renal function one year or longer after cessation of treatment.
Review article discussing genetic regulation and mechanisms of cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function in childhood cancer survivors.
Methodological study reexpressing the MDRD equation for standardized serum creatinine. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment.

Study of 536 children with various renal pathologies comparing GFR estimation formulas. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment. Does not meet population or intervention criteria.

Study of 90 patients with bilateral Wilms tumor reporting on treatment outcomes and survival. Does not specifically report on renal function outcomes (GFR, proteinuria, etc.). Focus is on tumor response and survival, not renal late effects.
Study of 1289 adult survivors of testicular cancer evaluating blood pressure and BMI. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.
Review article discussing biology and treatment of pediatric osteosarcoma. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.

Retrospective review of 12 articles (1108 patients) evaluating late renal toxicity after TBI/chemotherapy conditioning for BMT. Includes pediatric population subgroup. Reports on renal complications related to TBI dose, dose rate, and chemotherapy. Meets criteria: includes childhood cancer survivors, radiation involving kidney region, >20 participants, renal outcomes reported.
Review article discussing organ-sparing approaches in pediatric renal and testicular tumors. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.

Study of 324 childhood acute leukemia survivors reporting on late effects including hypertension, cardiac abnormalities, etc. Does not specifically report on renal function outcomes (GFR, proteinuria, tubular function). Focus is on general late effects, not renal-specific outcomes.

Study of 64 pediatric BMT patients (mean age 7.6 years) with follow-up 2 months to 11 years. Reports on renal insufficiency rates (50% early, 28% late). TBI conditioning involves kidney region. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, radiation involving kidney region, >20 participants, renal outcomes reported.

Large cohort study of 1362 childhood cancer survivors assessing total burden of adverse health outcomes. Does not specifically report on renal function outcomes. Focus is on overall adverse events, not renal-specific outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment.

Study of 42 children undergoing BMT with renal function assessed before and immediately after conditioning regimen. Does not report on renal function ≥1 year after treatment cessation. Focus is on acute/subacute renal changes after conditioning.
Study evaluating gonadal function after BMT in children. Does not report on renal function outcomes. Focus is on ovarian and testicular function, not renal outcomes.

Study of 53 Wilms tumor survivors with mean follow-up 13 years. Reports on renal dysfunction (32%), including low GFR (19%), hypertension (11%), and increased urinary albumin (9%). Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrectomy treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.
Study of 71 adult patients undergoing partial nephrectomy for renal tumors. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

Study of 25 Hodgkin patients receiving radiotherapy to retroperitoneal lymph nodes. Reports on renal function tests. However, population is not specified as children, and study appears to be in adults. Does not clearly meet population criteria for childhood cancer survivors.

Study of 32 patients (age 6-35.6 years) with intracranial germinoma. Reports on neurological and endocrinological deficiencies but not renal function outcomes. Does not report on renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment.

Study of 30 infants receiving cisplatin. While GFR was measured at end of treatment in 29 children, only 10 were retested at follow-up. Sample size of 10 with long-term renal outcome data is fewer than 20 participants. Does not meet minimum sample size criterion for long-term outcomes.

Study of 174 children receiving ifosfamide for various cancers. Assessed at multiple timepoints including 5 years after treatment. Reports on tubular and glomerular dysfunction with multivariable analysis identifying age and cumulative dose as risk factors. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, ifosfamide treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.

Meta-analysis comparing diagnostic accuracy of cystatin C vs serum creatinine for detecting renal dysfunction. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment. Does not meet population or intervention criteria.

Study of 763 adult survivors of childhood cancer with median follow-up 18.3 years. Reports on eGFR, albuminuria, and tubular function. Identifies nephrectomy, abdominal radiotherapy, high-dose ifosfamide, and high-dose cisplatin as associated with renal impairment. Meets all criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrotoxic treatments, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.
Study of adult patients with renal cancer comparing surgically induced CKD vs medical CKD. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

Study of 40 children assessed at least 18 months (median 2.5 years) after cisplatin treatment cessation. Reports on GFR measurements showing partial recovery from cisplatin glomerular toxicity. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, cisplatin treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.

Prospective study of 593 children/adolescents with sarcoma treated with ifosfamide. Median follow-up 19 months. Reports on tubulopathy incidence (4.6%) and identifies cumulative dose and young age as risk factors via multivariate analysis. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, ifosfamide treatment, >20 participants, renal outcomes reported >1 year post-treatment.
Review article discussing nephrotoxicity of cancer treatment in children. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.
Study of 100 adult patients (mean age 44 years) receiving cisplatin. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.
Study of 109 adult patients with small renal tumors undergoing partial nephrectomy. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

RCT of 55 subjects undergoing TBI-HSCT evaluating captopril for preventing chronic renal failure. Population not specified as children. Does not clearly meet population criteria for childhood cancer survivors.

Study of 349 children with chronic kidney disease developing new GFR estimating equations. Not focused on childhood cancer survivors or renal outcomes after nephrotoxic treatment. Does not meet population or intervention criteria.

Study of 25 patients with bilateral Wilms tumor reporting on treatment outcomes and survival. States 'no renal failure or any therapy-related complications were reported' but does not provide detailed renal function data (GFR, proteinuria, etc.). Does not report on renal function outcomes.

Study of 258 children including 92 receiving chemotherapy and 108 long-term survivors. Reports on cystatin C levels (glomerular function marker) after cisplatin, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, and multimodality treatment. Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrotoxic treatments, >20 participants, renal function reported.
Methodological guidelines for reporting observational studies. Not a primary research study with data on renal function in childhood cancer survivors.

Study of 23 patients with bilateral Wilms tumor undergoing nephron-sparing surgery. 12 survivors with follow-up 1-15 years reported preserved renal function (lowest GFR 65 ml/min/1.73m2). Meets criteria: childhood cancer survivors, nephrectomy treatment, >20 participants, renal function assessed >1 year post-treatment.

Study of 79 patients receiving allogeneic BMT with TBI conditioning. Reports on renal dysfunction-free survival at 18 months. However, population is not specified as children. Does not clearly meet population criteria for childhood cancer survivors.
Study of 131 adult patients undergoing nephroureterectomy. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.
Article presenting clinical vignettes of childhood cancer survivors for primary care physicians. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.
Review article discussing delayed consequences of childhood cancer therapy, focusing on growth effects. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.
Review article describing methods for assessing chemotherapy-associated nephrotoxicity in children. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.

Study of only 9 pediatric patients who survived >5 years after TBI/HSCT. Reports on eGFR changes with median follow-up 140 months. However, sample size of 9 is fewer than 20 participants. Does not meet minimum sample size criterion.

Study of 37 patients undergoing partial nephrectomy and 770 undergoing total nephrectomy for unilateral Wilms tumor. Reports on survival and relapse rates but does not report on renal function outcomes (GFR, proteinuria, etc.). Focus is on oncologic outcomes, not renal late effects.
Study of 27 adult patients with metastatic melanoma receiving IL-2 and cisplatin. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

Study of 52 children with unilateral localized Wilms tumor comparing nephron sparing surgery vs simple nephrectomy. Reports on survival and local recurrence rates but does not report on renal function outcomes. Focus is on oncologic outcomes, not renal late effects.

Report from the National Wilms Tumor Study evaluating treatment strategies for Wilms tumor. Reports on survival and relapse rates but does not report on renal function outcomes. Focus is on oncologic outcomes, not renal late effects.
Letter to the editor with no abstract available. Not a primary research study with sufficient data for screening. Cannot assess eligibility based on available information.
Study of 4180 adult patients undergoing surgery for renal malignancy. Not childhood cancer survivors. Does not meet population criteria.

Study evaluating somatic growth and renal function after unilateral nephrectomy for Wilms tumor. Reports on DTPA clearance and microalbuminuria (84% of patients). Childhood cancer survivors with nephrectomy treatment. Conservative inclusion as it reports on renal function outcomes, though sample size is unclear from abstract.

Study of 124 patients with previously treated sarcoma receiving ifosfamide and mesna. Population appears to be adults (not specified as children). Reports on neurotoxicity and hematuria but not on long-term renal function outcomes ≥1 year after treatment. Does not meet population or outcome criteria.
Review article discussing renal toxicity of ifosfamide and cisplatin in children. Not a primary research study with original data on renal function outcomes.

Study about parathyroid cysts in adults undergoing thyroidectomy/parathyroidectomy. Not related to childhood cancer or nephrotoxic treatments.
Study focuses on cardiovascular disease risk factors in brain cancer survivors. No assessment of renal function reported.
Pediatric patients after autologous BMT with TBI. Reports GFR, ERPF, concentrating capacity at median 10 years follow-up. TBI involves kidneys and may cause nephrotoxicity. n=40 patients.
Children nephrectomized for Wilms tumor (n=22) and hydronephrosis (n=15). Assessed GFR long-term after nephrectomy. Meets criteria for nephrectomy exposure.

79 patients treated with ifosfamide, some with cisplatin/radiotherapy/nephrectomy. Assessed proximal tubular function. However, only 10 developed syndrome - unclear if full cohort assessed. May be borderline.
Survival study of malignant rhabdoid tumors. Focuses on event-free survival and overall survival, not renal function outcomes.
Review article describing late effects in childhood cancer survivors. Not an original study reporting specific renal function data.
Randomized trial in patients with solid tumors (not specified as pediatric). Only 31 patients total. Follow-up during treatment, not ≥1 year after cessation.
Prospective longitudinal study of 25 children treated with ifosfamide. Assessed GFR, phosphate, bicarbonate at end of treatment, 1 year, and 10 years. Meets all criteria.
Bilateral Wilms tumor patients (n=36), 8 had repeat NSS. Assessed renal function with average 4.5 year follow-up. Nephrectomy exposure present.
Pediatric patients after TBI and HSCT (n=39 with follow-up, mean 8.3 years). Examined cardiac, pulmonary, and renal function. 5 exhibited renal impairment.
Postmortem examination study comparing allo-SCT recipients with controls. Not a clinical study of renal function in survivors.
Study of osteosarcoma survival trends over 30 years. Mentions late cardiac effects and secondary malignancies but does not report specific renal function outcomes.
Cross-sectional study of metabolic syndrome in 55 ALL survivors. Focuses on insulin resistance, obesity, lipids. No renal function assessment.
Review article discussing compensatory kidney growth after nephrectomy. References other studies but does not present original data on childhood cancer survivors.
Pharmacokinetic study of melphalan in 59 children. Uses GFR as covariate but does not assess renal function as outcome of interest.
Preliminary results of preoperative chemotherapy for Wilms tumor. Focuses on stage distribution and survival, not renal function outcomes.
Large study of cardiovascular risk factors in 8599 survivors. Does not report renal function outcomes.
Phase II trial of carboplatin for retinoblastoma (n=25). States 'no non-hematopoietic serious or permanent toxicities' observed. No renal function assessment.
Summary report of SIOP clinical trials from 1971-1980. Discusses treatment strategies and survival, not renal function outcomes.
HSCT study in 123 pediatric ALL patients. Mentions renal failure in 11% as acute complication but does not assess long-term renal function ≥1 year after treatment.
Review article on genetic causes of hypomagnesemia. Not an original study of childhood cancer survivors.
Study of 30 adults undergoing nephrectomy for renal cell carcinoma. Not childhood cancer population.
42 patients with synchronous bilateral Wilms tumor. All had eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m² at last follow-up (mean 4.1 years). Nephrectomy exposure with renal function assessment.
75 patients with unilateral Wilms tumor treated with nephrectomy without nephrotoxic chemo or radiation. Median follow-up 19.6 years. Assessed eGFR and hypertension.
43 osteosarcoma patients aged 4-34 years (median 16). Pediatric subgroup analyzed separately. Assessed renal function at median 16 months post-treatment. Includes high-dose ifosfamide and cisplatin.
Study of 31 high-risk neuroblastoma patients receiving IORT. Focuses on local control and survival. Mentions hypertension/vascular stenosis in 7 patients but no renal function assessment.
Retrospective cohort of 180 HCT recipients (adults and pediatrics). Focuses on hypertension and diabetes, not renal function outcomes.
33 Wilms tumor patients with unilateral nephrectomy (23 evaluable). Treated with non-nephrotoxic drugs. Mean follow-up 4.6 years. Assessed GFR by inulin clearance.
Review article on acute leukemia diagnosis and management in children. Not an original study with renal function data.
Book chapter on endocrinopathy after childhood cancer treatment. Review material, not original research.

Randomized trial of 856 Ewing sarcoma patients comparing cyclophosphamide vs ifosfamide. Reports acute tubular toxicities (16% vs 31%). Long-term renal toxicity evaluation ongoing but acute data available.
Review article on health status and late complications after allogeneic BMT. Mentions impaired renal function early post-transplant but not original data.
Review article on cisplatin-induced hypomagnesemia. Discusses mechanisms and management but not original study data.
Retrospective review of 19 high-risk osteosarcoma patients receiving HDCT/ASCT. Small sample size (<20). Focuses on survival outcomes, not renal function.
Case series of 5 Wilms tumor patients who developed Fanconi syndrome after ifosfamide. Sample size <20, appears to be case series format.
Review article on ifosfamide nephrotoxicity mechanisms and prevention. Not original research data.
32 long-term survivors (>10 years) of neuroblastoma and Wilms tumor. Kidney radionuclide scans performed. Marked renal impairment detected in 2 NRB patients.
Study of 32 patients with neuroendocrine tumors receiving In-111 pentetreotide. Adult population, not childhood cancer.
Review article/guide for radiologists on cancer therapy complications. Educational material, not original research.
Study of 31 Wilms tumor survivors focusing on bone mineral density. Mentions possible subtle renal tubular defect but primary outcome is osteopenia, not renal function.
25 children with solid tumors treated with ifosfamide. Assessed glomerular and tubular function. Urinary beta-2 microglobulin elevated in 11 patients. Follow-up one year.
Clinical practice guidelines for adolescent and young adult oncology. Not original research study.
Population-based survival study of 157,499 children. Focuses on survival rates, not renal function outcomes.
Summary of SIGN guidance on long-term follow-up of childhood cancer survivors. Guidance document, not original research.
German language review article on Wilms tumor diagnosis and therapy. Mentions late effects but not original data.
Cross-sectional study of 1442 survivors ≥5 years after diagnosis. Assessed eGFR, albuminuria, hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatemia, BP. Median follow-up 12.1 years.
76 Wilms tumor patients after nephrectomy. Mean follow-up 9.0 years. Assessed protein/creatinine index and GFR correlation.
Commentary/editorial on ifosfamide/mesna continuous infusion regimen. Discusses another study but not original research data.
Study of 36 BMT patients measuring serum erythropoietin levels. Mentions nephrotoxicity but not primary renal function assessment.
